channel.title: Nature Communications
channel.description:
Nature Communications is an open access, multidisciplinary journal dedicated to publishing high-quality research in all areas of the biological, health, physical, chemical and Earth sciences. Papers published by the journal aim to represent important advances of significance to specialists within each field.

We are committed to providing an efficient service for both authors and readers. Our team of independent editors make rapid and fair publication decisions. Prompt dissemination of accepted papers to a wide readership and beyond is achieved through a programme of continuous online publication.

item.title: A neural circuit of food sight-promoted feeding and contextual memory in mice
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 11 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77682-y

Feeding can be regulated by sensory cues. This study identifies a multi-layer circuit that mediates food sight-promoted feeding and food-related memory in mice.
item.dc:title: A neural circuit of food sight-promoted feeding and contextual memory in mice

item.title: SLC4A7/NBCn1 maintains intracellular pH to support mTORC1 activity and antibody-secreting cell differentiation
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 11 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77588-9

Environmental cues, such as pH, determine cellular differentiation and function, including that of immune cells. Here the authors identify SLC4A7, a Na + /HCO3–cotransporter as a critical and specific regulator of plasmablast differentiation genetic deletion of which in mice impairing antibody responses.
item.dc:title: SLC4A7/NBCn1 maintains intracellular pH to support mTORC1 activity and antibody-secreting cell differentiation

item.title: Discovery of an antagonist nanobody targeting the oxytocin receptor with tocolytic effect in mice
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 11 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77680-0

Preterm birth poses severe risks to mothers and newborns. Here, the authors identify an oxytocin receptor antagonist nanobody with tocolytic effects in mice, offering a potential roadmap for developing next generation tocolytic drugs.
item.dc:title: Discovery of an antagonist nanobody targeting the oxytocin receptor with tocolytic effect in mice

item.title: Predictability can be dynamically constructed in deterministic systems
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 11 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77737-0

In a deterministic, non-chaotic system, the initial state fixes the future completely, yet that future may be impossible to forecast from it. Using a cellular automaton of communicating cells, this study shows that predictability is instead built by the dynamics: collective topological structures self-organize as the system evolves, and only once they exist does the eventual outcome become legible.
item.dc:title: Predictability can be dynamically constructed in deterministic systems

item.title: CReP-mediated control of eIF2α phosphorylation is a critical node in MYC-driven medulloblastoma
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 11 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77565-2

Group 3 (G3) medulloblastoma is an aggressive paediatric brain tumour with limited treatment options. Here, the authors show that CReP phosphatase maintains eIF2α activity, thereby protecting G3 MB cells from apoptosis, and that these cells are sensitive to eIF2α inactivation.
item.dc:title: CReP-mediated control of eIF2α phosphorylation is a critical node in MYC-driven medulloblastoma

item.title: Selective O<sub>3</sub>/SPC oxidation minimizes the carbon footprint of concentrated aromatic remediation via in situ endogenous carbon
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 11 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77676-w

The study presents a selective oxidation strategy using ozone and sodium percarbonate to transform recalcitrant aromatics in pesticide wastewater into biodegradable nutrients. The process enables self-sufficient biological treatment and lowers the carbon footprint by 40%, advancing sustainable remediation.
item.dc:title: Selective O<sub>3</sub>/SPC oxidation minimizes the carbon footprint of concentrated aromatic remediation via in situ endogenous carbon

item.title: Co-optimized volumetric muscle design for large dynamic deformations in versatile biohybrid robots
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 11 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77655-1

The authors combine computer simulation and experimental fabrication to co-design living muscle and its scaffold, optimizing the range of motion of bioactuators to power biohybrid robots that can jump, swim, walk and grip.
item.dc:title: Co-optimized volumetric muscle design for large dynamic deformations in versatile biohybrid robots

item.title: Mitigating tin ion migration and reinforcing buried interface via synergistic polymer-modified tin oxide
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 11 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77624-8

The buried interface in perovskite solar cells is vulnerable to light-induced degradation but difficult to probe. Yang et al. reveal a role of tin migration in accelerating degradation and use polymer interlayers to reinforce the interface, improving device performance and stability.
item.dc:title: Mitigating tin ion migration and reinforcing buried interface via synergistic polymer-modified tin oxide
